title: Rune's Sunny Surprise
markdown:
The air in Willow Creek buzzed like happy bumblebees. Colourful ribbons fluttered on lampposts. Apple pies, berry tarts, and toasty nuts tickled noses and made tummies rumble. Harvest Fair: the garden’s yummy goodness, all in one square.

Young Rune, a wizard with hair like sun-dried straw and eyes as bright as polished acorns, stood by the big fountain, spellbook in his hands. It smelled of old paper, dried leaves, and sleepy moonlight. Today his job was simple: a little weather magic. Charm the sunbeams. Whisper a gentle breeze, just right for the fair. “A soft breeze, a warm sun,” he had practiced, voice a clear happy tune.

His two best friends had come to wish him luck. Nessa the otter, fur shiny like a wet river stone, sat on the fountain’s mossy edge polishing a smooth grey pebble with her nose. Clover the robin, on a branch just above, chirped a song like tiny bells.

“Ready, Rune?” Clover trilled.

“Almost!” His spectacles kept slipping. “Just one more word, and the fair will be perfectly, wonderfully sunny!” He puffed out his chest like a proud little bird and began to chant. A faint shimmer, like heat rising from a meadow, hummed around him.

Nessa’s sharp ears heard a funny sound. Not a soft whoosh of breeze. Drip, drip, drip. Clover’s song faltered. “That’s a funny sound for rain.”

The shimmering light grew brighter, but it was not warm and golden. It was silvery, and it seemed to get wetter. Nessa slid into the fountain with a happy splish-splash. “Rune! That doesn’t sound like a sunny-day charm at all!”

Rune blinked, spectacles fogging. “But I’m saying it just like it’s written!” The pages looked a bit smudged, as if a tiny cloud had wept upon them.

Clover fluttered down onto the open page. “Oh dearie me! You’ve said ‘drench’ instead of ‘dance’! And ‘downpour’ instead of ‘dewdrop’! And that big word? It’s ‘deluge,’ not ‘delight’!”

Rune’s cheerful smile drooped like a wilting flower. “I’m going to drench the fair? With a deluge?” He pictured soggy pies, puddles in the puppet tent, ribbons hanging like sad limp noodles. Worse than a pot of ink on a favourite drawing.

Nessa pointed her nose at the centre of the fountain. “The old stories say the fountain remembers everything. Especially important things for Willow Creek.” She nudged a loose tile. “Look!”

Underneath, a hidden space. Etched on a smooth flat stone: more words, but different, with little pictures like a fairy’s notebook—a bright sun, a plump berry, a happy face.

“This looks like the real charm!” Clover hopped closer. “A Sunbeam Sprinkle! It’s meant to make the harvested berries extra, extra sweet for all the delicious tarts!”

Rune’s spellbook was a copy. Someone had made tiny wiggly mistakes writing it down. His mix-up had not only promised rain; it had almost ruined the promise of the sweetest berries in Willow Creek. Without the Sprinkle, the famous tarts would be pale and watery.

A shiver swept through him. Cheerful music started from the bandstand. “How do we fix it?”

Nessa looked at the stone. “It’s like a riddle. ‘Where the water laughs and the sunbeams play, the sweetest secret will show you the way.’” She nudged a jet from a carved fish’s mouth. “The water laughs—the fountain spray. The sunbeams play—where the light dances on the water.”

They peered in. Sunbeams hit splashing water and made a dazzling dance. Near where water poured from a little stone bird’s beak, a tiny glowing symbol appeared: sweetness.

“That’s it!” Rune traced it, feeling smooth coolness. “Not just keeping rain away. Making the berries wonderfully sweet.”

He pulled out a fresh piece of soft paper and a quill, dipped in shimmering golden ink. As the band played a happy tune, he copied every sunbeam and every hint of sweetness. He closed his eyes, took a calm breath, and cast the real spell. His voice was sure, steady, warm like summer. Soft golden light, like honey pouring from a jar, spread from Rune and bathed the square. Not a downpour. Not a chilly breeze. Sunshine and hopeful harvest.

Nessa dipped a paw into the spray. “It’s sparkly!” she giggled, licking her whiskers.

Clover nipped a berry from a nearby stall. Eyes widened. “Oh, Rune! They’re already tasting sweeter!”

Townsfolk cheered, faces bright, not knowing how close the tarts had come to bland. Music swelled. Laughter echoed. Rune’s spectacles sat straight for once. Nessa’s pebble gleamed. Clover’s bellsong found the fountain’s splash and, for a moment, they matched.
characters: Nessa (an otter), Rune (a young wizard), Clover (a robin)
